title: 四级：安静展厅与周转箱两篇阅读
instruction: Read both passages and choose the best answer to each question. 每篇五题，每题只选一项；全部材料与问题均需作答。
source_notice: 参照已核考试院2016大纲及完整样题：每篇五题、每题四候选，四级每篇300—350词、六级400—450词；单篇完整练习与整节两篇十题分列，不把单篇冒充整节。本文城镇、机构、人物、事件与研究均为原创虚构，按文意作答，不作现实事实。旧官方样题原键既有风险保留，不当独立gold；本稿逐项依据与干扰反证为作者自审，独立教研、学生、商用及生产未验证，不证明产品档位人群等值。

passages.text:
A small museum in the fictional town of Denhurst reopened with a feature that surprised some visitors: a room without automatic sound effects. Elsewhere, recorded voices and music accompanied displays. In the quiet room, visitors could read about ordinary objects and choose whether to hear a recording through headphones. Silence, rather than continuous sound, was the starting point.

The change came after a family described leaving an earlier exhibition halfway through. One child had enjoyed the objects but found the sudden noises distressing. Museum staff initially considered offering a separate visit before normal opening hours. The family explained that travelling at that time would be difficult. They wanted more control over sound during an ordinary visit, not merely an invitation to arrive earlier.

The museum therefore tested individual listening devices beside a display of kitchen tools. A visitor could pick up a recording or continue reading without it. Staff supplied written versions of the recordings and made sure that essential information appeared on the display itself. Choosing silence would not mean missing the explanation that made an object understandable.

Some regular visitors feared that the exhibition would become dull. The curator replied that the museum was adding a choice, rather than forbidding lively experiences. Other rooms still included group demonstrations. The quiet room offered a different pace, and visitors could move between the two. A person seeking calm did not have to leave the museum altogether.

The arrangement also changed staff duties. Instead of simply switching on a sound system each morning, they checked the headphones, replaced damaged written sheets and helped visitors find the version they preferred. The curator regarded this work as part of the exhibition, not as an optional kindness. A choice advertised at the entrance was useful only if people could actually exercise it inside. People could make that decision without asking staff to silence an entire room.

options: It excludes every recording and written explanation.
It requires visitors to listen before examining objects.
It allows visitors to choose recorded sound individually.
It is available only before the museum opens.
questions.evidence: Silence, rather than continuous sound, was the starting point

candidate_reasons.A: 可选耳机且有文字，非全无
candidate_reasons.C: 默认安静、个人选择耳机，C正确
candidate_reasons.D: 普通开放期间可访，非限定提前

questions.stem: Why did the family find the first suggestion inadequate?
options: The proposed visiting time would be difficult for them.
They objected to every form of kitchen display.
They preferred louder automatic sound effects.
They wanted the whole museum closed to other visitors.
questions.evidence: travelling at that time would be difficult

candidate_reasons.A: 提前到馆交通时间困难，A直接支持
candidate_reasons.B: 孩子喜爱展品，未反厨具
candidate_reasons.C: 孩子困扰于噪声，非想更大声

questions.stem: Why was essential information printed on the display?
options: To prevent staff from changing any exhibition labels.
To persuade all visitors to stop listening to recordings.
To keep the display understandable when visitors chose silence.
questions.evidence: Choosing silence would not mean missing the explanation

candidate_reasons.C: 提供选择，不劝全员弃听
candidate_reasons.D: 不听也不漏理解必需解释，D正确

questions.stem: How did the curator address concerns about dullness?
options: By removing all group demonstrations from other rooms.
By explaining that the quiet room expanded the range of experiences.
By reserving the quiet room only for the family that complained.
By requiring lively visitors to remain outside the museum.
questions.evidence: adding a choice, rather than forbidding lively experiences

candidate_reasons.B: 静与动可切换，是选择扩展
candidate_reasons.C: 全体访客可选，非一家专用

questions.stem: What does the final paragraph emphasise?
options: Staff can withdraw advertised choices whenever maintenance is difficult.
Providing headphones automatically removes the need for visitor support.
Maintaining practical access is part of delivering the exhibition.
Written sheets should replace the museum’s other exhibits.
questions.evidence: A choice advertised at the entrance was useful only if people could actually exercise it inside

candidate_reasons.A: 把维护视为展览组成，非随意撤回
candidate_reasons.B: 明确新增帮助与维护工作
candidate_reasons.C: 承诺选择需落实维护与辅助，C概括
candidate_reasons.D: 文字是提供信息的版本，非取代其他展品

passages.text:
A fictional vegetable supplier, Green Basket, replaced disposable delivery boxes with reusable crates. Each crate was stronger than a cardboard box and could be folded when empty. The company expected its drivers to collect yesterday’s crates while delivering today’s orders. Managers calculated that repeated use would reduce the number of new boxes they needed to buy.

The first difficulty appeared at small restaurants. Deliveries arrived before breakfast, but cooks did not always empty the crates immediately. Drivers could not wait while vegetables were moved into storage. A crate that was theoretically reusable might therefore remain in a kitchen for several days. Meanwhile, the supplier needed another one for the next delivery.

Customers suggested leaving their empty crates outside overnight. That helped collections, but some restaurants had no secure outdoor space. Others shared an entrance with flats, whose residents objected to a growing stack beside the door. There was no single collection arrangement that suited every customer, even though the containers themselves were identical.

Green Basket responded by discussing return times when restaurants placed orders. Larger kitchens agreed to weekly collections, while some smaller ones chose a brief afternoon visit. The company also offered an ordinary cardboard box where a return system was impractical. It did not describe customers choosing that option as careless: their buildings and working hours could make a difference.

A later review counted crates still at customers’ premises as well as those ready for another journey. The change made the apparent saving less impressive than the original forecast. Yet it also showed managers where more containers or better collection routes were needed. They kept the scheme, but stopped treating the durability of a crate as sufficient evidence that it would circulate efficiently. The object could be reused; the work needed to return it still had to be organised.

questions.stem: What assumption lay behind the original plan?
options: Restaurants would stop buying vegetables before breakfast.
Empty crates could be collected during the next delivery.
Each crate would be used only once before disposal.
Drivers would unload every restaurant’s vegetables personally.
questions.evidence: collect yesterday’s crates while delivering today’s orders

candidate_reasons.A: 早餐前是交货时间，非停止订菜
candidate_reasons.B: 次日送货同时收旧箱，B正确
candidate_reasons.D: 司机不能等，不承诺亲自卸每箱

questions.stem: Why did some crates remain in restaurants?
options: The crates could not be folded after use.
Cooks had been instructed to keep them as kitchen furniture.
Vegetables were not always removed before the driver needed to leave.
Restaurants had stopped receiving regular deliveries.
questions.evidence: cooks did not always empty the crates immediately

candidate_reasons.C: 未及时腾空且司机不能等，C是原因

questions.stem: What does “circulate” in the final paragraph mean?
options: Move through repeated deliveries and returns.
Remain permanently in one customer’s kitchen.
Expand into a larger container when emptied.

candidate_reasons.A: 循环送达并回收再用，A符合整篇流程
candidate_reasons.B: 留在厨房是循环受阻，不是circulate
candidate_reasons.C: 耐用是物性，并非流转含义
candidate_reasons.D: 空箱可折叠，不膨胀变大

questions.stem: Why did the company retain a cardboard option?
options: To punish customers who returned crates too slowly.
To hide the costs of reusable containers from managers.
To discourage larger kitchens from arranging weekly collections.
To accommodate customers for whom returns were difficult to organise.
questions.evidence: where a return system was impractical

candidate_reasons.B: 复核公开了在外箱数，非隐藏
candidate_reasons.C: 大型厨房已约周收，未劝阻
candidate_reasons.D: 建筑与工时使回收不可行，D准确

questions.stem: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Durability alone guarantees the success of any return scheme.
Reusable packaging requires a workable system of collection.
Forecasts should ignore containers held at customers’ premises.
All customers must use an identical collection schedule.
questions.evidence: the work needed to return it still had to be organised

candidate_reasons.B: 物件可重复利用但回运需组织，B概括
candidate_reasons.D: 方案因客户而异，不同排程
